title: Accessibility
summary: Shows the system accessibility settings that Bipe follows and the current state of each one. Bipe has no own switch for them: the screen sends the person to the system settings and to the accessibility page on bipe.chat.

title.description: String key of the setting name: bipe_accessibility_screen_reader, bipe_accessibility_text_size, bipe_accessibility_reduce_motion or bipe_accessibility_contrast.

value.description: String key of the current state: bipe_accessibility_on or bipe_accessibility_off; for textSize bipe_accessibility_text_default, bipe_accessibility_text_larger or bipe_accessibility_text_smaller.

items.description: All four settings, in the order of the setting enum.

openSystemSettings.effect: Android only: opens the system accessibility settings (Settings.ACTION_ACCESSIBILITY_SETTINGS).

openAccessibilityPage.effect: Opens urls.accessibility of registries/settings.json in the in-app browser, in the app language.

notes: Opens from the row accessibility in Conversas e mídia (registries/settings.json, bipe-chat/bipe#917).
Order: the intro text, the four info rows, then the system button (Android) or the path footer (iOS), then the page row.
The rows show state only and have no action. A second switch in Bipe could disagree with the system setting.
The state updates when the person changes a system setting and comes back to the screen.
Each info row reads as one element for VoiceOver and TalkBack: the name, then the state.

iOS sources: UIAccessibility.isVoiceOverRunning; accessibilityReduceMotion; colorSchemeContrast == .increased; dynamicTypeSize (.large is the default). iOS has no public URL to the Accessibility pane of Settings, so iOS shows bipe_accessibility_ios_path as the footer and has no system button.

Android sources: AccessibilityManager.isTouchExplorationEnabled; the animator duration scale (common/Motion.kt reduceMotion); the contrast level and High contrast text (BipeTheme.kt highContrast); the font scale (1.0 is the default).
